issues.legal_issue: A writing that records an agreement to sell and contemplates a later formal conveyance is an agreement rather than a completed sale and is admissible as such.
material_facts: The writing set out terms of the proposed sale and referred to execution of a sale deed on registered paper in the future.
A separate registered conveyance was executed later.
issues.conclusion: The writing was a contract of sale, not a completed sale, and was admissible as an agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The distinction between a contract of sale and an actual sale turns on the instrument's terms and the parties' contemplation of a later conveyance; a contract of sale creates no interest in or charge on the property. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.document_records_agreed_sale_terms: The parties recorded the terms of an agreed sale in a document.
predicates.document_contemplates_later_formal_conve: The document contemplated that the parties would complete the transfer through a later formal conveyance.
predicates.document_is_admissible_as_a_sale_agreeme: The document is admissible as evidence of a sale agreement rather than as a completed sale.

issues.definition: When a document records agreed sale terms and contemplates a later formal conveyance, it is admissible as a sale agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A genuine earlier contract to purchase prevails over a later contract made by the same vendor unless the earlier purchaser is estopped from asserting that contract.
material_facts: The courts below concurrently found that the earlier purchaser's contract was genuine and concluded before the other purchaser's contract.
The earlier purchaser later obtained a registered conveyance.
The other purchaser's contract arose later and was conditional on the vendor being able to make out a good title.
The earlier purchaser protested the proposed later transaction, and the Court found no proof of consent or acquiescence.
issues.conclusion: The later contract could not prevail over the earlier purchaser's contract, and the earlier purchaser was not estopped from asserting it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a later claimant under the vendor could not displace the earlier purchaser's contract in the absence of estoppel. Under Section 27 of the Specific Relief Act, a purchaser under an earlier contract could seek specific performance against the vendor and a person claiming under a title arising subsequently to that contract. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_a_decree and genuine_earlier_purchase_contract and later_claim_arises_under_same_vendor and no_estoppel_against_earlier_purchaser

predicates.civil_appeal_from_a_decree: The proceeding is a civil appeal from a decree concerning competing claims to property.
predicates.genuine_earlier_purchase_contract: A court finds that one purchaser made a genuine contract to purchase before a competing purchaser's contract.
predicates.later_claim_arises_under_same_vendor: The competing claimant bases the later claim on a transaction with the same vendor.
predicates.no_estoppel_against_earlier_purchaser: The earlier purchaser did not consent to or acquiesce in the later transaction in a way that bars assertion of the earlier contract.
predicates.earlier_purchase_contract_prevails_over_: The earlier purchaser's claim prevails over the competing claim arising later through the same vendor.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal from a decree, a genuine earlier purchase contract prevails over a later claim through the same vendor when the earlier purchaser is not estopped from asserting it.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser is not estopped from asserting an earlier contract merely because the purchaser was near the vendor when a later transaction was made, where the evidence does not establish consent or acquiescence.
material_facts: The earlier purchaser was in the same city as the vendor when the later contract was made.
The earlier purchaser sent a telegram asserting the prior purchase and objecting to a further sale without consent.
The Court found no proof that the earlier purchaser consented to or acquiesced in the later transaction.
issues.conclusion: The earlier purchaser was not estopped from asserting rights under the prior contract.
issues.legal_principle: Estoppel required proof of conduct amounting to consent or acquiescence; mere presence with the vendor was insufficient. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.earlier_purchase_contract_exists: The purchaser had made a contract to buy the property before the competing transaction.
predicates.purchaser_was_near_vendor_during_later_t: The purchaser was in the vendor's company or location when the later transaction was made.
predicates.purchaser_protested_or_no_acquiescence_w: The purchaser objected to the later transaction, or the evidence failed to establish the purchaser's acquiescence in it.
predicates.purchaser_is_not_estopped_from_asserting: The purchaser is not barred from asserting rights under the earlier contract.

issues.definition: A purchaser who had an earlier contract is not estopped by mere proximity to the vendor during a later transaction when the purchaser protested or acquiescence was not proved.

issues.legal_issue: Entry by a competing purchaser's representative does not establish that an earlier purchaser voluntarily surrendered possession when the earlier purchaser's representative did not consent to the transfer of possession.
material_facts: The earlier purchaser's representative took possession of the factories on the purchaser's behalf.
The competing purchaser's representative later entered the premises on the vendor's instructions.
The earlier purchaser's representative continued to frequent the premises, said that possession had not been given up, and protested the transfer.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not establish a consensual dispossession of the earlier purchaser's representative.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the evidence of possession and held that any dispossession was not with the representative's consent. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.possession_was_delivered_to_purchaser_re: The purchaser's representative received possession of the property on the purchaser's behalf.
predicates.competing_representative_later_entered: A competing claimant's representative later entered or took control of the property.
predicates.purchaser_representative_did_not_consent: The purchaser's representative did not agree to give up possession to the competing claimant.
predicates.possession_was_not_voluntarily_surrender: The purchaser's representative did not voluntarily surrender possession.

issues.definition: When possession was delivered to a purchaser's representative and that representative did not consent to a competing representative's later entry, possession was not voluntarily surrendered.

issues.legal_issue: The protection for part performance does not enable a later claimant under a vendor to defeat an earlier purchaser's rights where the later claimant took the contract with notice and was not a bona fide transferee for value without notice.
material_facts: The earlier purchaser had a genuine contract that predated the competing purchaser's contract.
The competing purchaser's claim arose under a later contract with the vendor, and that purchaser knew of the earlier purchaser's rights.
The competing purchaser had only a contract of sale, not a completed sale, and had paid only part of the stated consideration.
The earlier purchaser obtained a registered conveyance.
issues.conclusion: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act did not apply to give the competing purchaser a defence against the earlier purchaser's claim.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act regulates rights and obligations arising from written contracts for transfer of immovable property and does not protect a person claiming under a title that arose before the contract. Its proviso preserves the rights of a transferee for consideration who takes in good faith without notice. The Court also relied on Section 27 of the Specific Relief Act, which permits a claim for specific performance against a vendor and a person claiming under a subsequent title. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: earlier_purchase_contract_exists and later_claimant_relies_on_part_performance and later_claimant_knew_of_earlier_contract and later_claimant_was_not_a_bona_fide_transferee_without_notice

predicates.earlier_purchase_contract_exists: A purchaser made a contract to buy the property before the competing claimant's transaction.
predicates.later_claimant_relies_on_part_performanc: A later claimant relies on conduct or payment under a written contract to assert rights in the property.
predicates.later_claimant_knew_of_earlier_contract: The later claimant had notice of the earlier purchaser's contract.
predicates.later_claimant_was_not_a_bona_fide_trans: The later claimant did not take as a good-faith transferee for consideration without notice of the earlier contract.
predicates.part_performance_defence_does_not_defeat: The later claimant cannot use part performance to defeat the earlier purchaser's rights.

issues.definition: A part-performance claim does not defeat an earlier purchaser's contract when the later claimant had notice of that contract and did not take as a good-faith transferee for consideration without notice.
